openQuestions: First-ever green CI run confirmed this session: https://github.com/kalibudz/pdfworkerz/actions/runs/36356246278 (all 11 jobs). Every run before it, going back to P0, was red -- three real bugs (numpy==2.5.3 has no Python 3.11 wheel; engine/fonts/match.py's extract_metrics crashed on an outline-less system font found on ubuntu-latest; a CLI test asserted against Rich-wrapped --help text that splits mid-flag on CI terminal widths) had been silently failing every run. Local checks never caught any of this because this sandbox's bare `mypy`/`ruff`/`pip` on PATH resolve to tool installs (some uv-tool-isolated) unrelated to the project's own dependency closure -- always use `python3 -m <tool>` here, matching the interpreter `pip install -e ".[dev]"` actually targets.

server/app.py now has a CORSMiddleware scoped to a loopback-origin regex (127.0.0.1/localhost/::1, any port) -- deliberately not a wildcard, but also deliberately permissive on port, reasoned through explicitly in this session's PROGRESS.md entry: safe because auth here is a header a browser never auto-attaches, unlike a cookie. Any future addition of cookie-based or credentialed auth to this server would need to revisit this reasoning before reusing the same permissive-by-port policy.

web/package.json pins pdfjs-dist==6.3.289 deliberately: versions >=5.6.83 <6.2.108 carry a public high-severity CVE (arbitrary JS execution opening a malicious PDF). npm audit is now gated in CI's security job -- re-run it by hand after ever changing this pin, don't just trust the version number looks recent enough.

web/src/polyfills.ts + web/src/pdf.worker.ts work around a real Map/WeakMap.prototype.getOrInsertComputed gap on an older browser engine (this sandbox's own pinned Playwright test browser, specifically) that current pdfjs-dist relies on. It's a no-op on any browser that already has the method natively, so it's not a workaround that needs revisiting as browsers catch up -- but if a *different* pdfjs-dist-version-induced browser incompatibility shows up later, don't assume it's the same issue; check what's actually missing the same way this one was found (grep the built bundle for the failing symbol).

viewer.ts's toolbar controls are disabled until the document has actually finished loading (a real race was found and fixed here, documented in code and in PROGRESS.md) -- any future addition to viewer.ts that adds a new interactive control needs the same discipline: attach the listener immediately, guard its body on `pdf` being loaded, don't rely on `.pw-viewer` existing in the DOM as a readiness signal.

tests/web/'s Playwright tests build on a *built* web/dist, never on `vite dev` -- if `web/dist` doesn't exist (no npm build run yet), the whole module is skipped (not failed), so a plain `pytest` run with no prior `npm run build` silently produces no UI-01/UI-06 evidence rather than an error. CI always builds first; a human running tests locally needs to remember to.
Re-verify iLovePDF / Nitro parity tags against the vendors' current feature pages before the first release
P1 and P2 were self-reviewed (builder and reviewer were the same session); an independent reviewer pass is still owed before calling either phase fully signed off
RTL scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) and CJK vertical writing mode are not supported for editing -- documented in tests/engine/test_font_cjk.py's module docstring, not attempted
fit=True (FNT-10) fragments a span's texttrace into one span per character, breaking a second edit's ability to find that text as one span -- defaults to False
FNT-09's kerning only reads legacy 'kern' tables, not GPOS pair positioning; no GSUB ligature substitution is attempted at all

font-name matching between texttrace and Page.get_fonts()/pikepdf goes through engine.fonts.match.normalize_font_name plus a containment-match fallback -- reuse this pattern rather than comparing font-name strings directly anywhere new

detect_blocks (engine/fonts/blocks.py) assumes its input span list is already in visual top-to-bottom order -- not guaranteed after an edit. Relevant once UI-02/UI-04 might re-run block detection on an already-edited page.

ReflowTextOp's overflow check runs before its require_tier check, so an overflowing edit is reported as overflow even when the font match is also weak -- both surface eventually with allow_overflow=True, but not in the most actionable order
